recipes.name: Savory Zucchini Muffins
ingredients_raw: 0.75 teaspoon hot pepper sauce (such as Tabasco®)

steps.text: Preheat oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Grease 16 muffin cups or line with paper liners.

Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a skillet over medium heat; cook and stir the onion and garlic in the hot oil until the onion is translucent, about 5 minutes. Stir in the sun-dried tomatoes and remove from heat; transfer to a food processor. Add the zucchini and roasted red pepper to the tomato mixture; pulse the mixture several times until finely chopped.
Stir the all-purpose flour, cornmeal, whole wheat flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt, pepper, basil, and oregano together in a bowl.

In a separate large bowl, beat the butter with the sugar until fluffy using an electric mixer; beat in the eggs, one at a time. Stir in the sour cream, milk, hot pepper sauce, and 1 tablespoon of olive oil.

Stir half the flour mixture into the butter mixture until almost incorporated; add the rest of the flour mixture and stir a few times just to mix. Stir in the zucchini mixture. Spoon the batter into the prepared muffin cups until nearly full. Sprinkle each muffin cup with about 1 teaspoon of shredded Parmesan cheese, if desired.
Bake the muffins in the preheated oven until golden brown, 35 to 40 minutes. Allow to cool for 10 minutes before removing from pans.

raw_recipe.headline: Savory Zucchini Muffins
raw_recipe.description: A savory muffin with zucchini, onion, roasted red peppers, and sun-dried tomatoes is a nice change from the usual sweet zucchini muffin.

review.reviewBody: Christine, I am SO excited to be the first reviewer of your recipe so that I can give it a good jump start by showering it with the praise it deserves! The recipe, granted, is very involved for a muffin and requires a lot of ingredients. Maybe this unfortunately makes people pass it by. But here is a perfect example of how the effort you put into something is SO worth the results! As the first reviewer I felt a responsibility to strictly stick to the recipe and other than using full fat sour cream and skipping the optional Parmesan topping, I did. As these were baking (mine only took 30 minutes) the aroma was so good it truly was making my mouth water - and I'm not being dramatic to stress a point! Healthy, flavorful ingredients and flecked with lovely colors, but the true test would be the taste test. You have outdone yourself! They are perfect! Moist, great texture, beautiful, and such a unique flavor! You have this recipe down pat, and I would strongly encourage others not only to try these, but to make them exactly as the recipe directs - that means no shortcuts, no changes, no substitutions or deletions. I can't imagine how this recipe could be improved upon the perfection it already is. Thank you for sharing your recipe!

This is a good recipe, easily modified.

I doubled the herbs and some powdered garlic and extra sea salt....otherwise these would have been bland for my tastes. Also used organic full fat yogurt rather than sour cream and almond milk rather than dairy.

Also used veggies I had on hand... broccoli + fresh bell pepper instead of dried tomatoes & roasted red pepper (sauteed with other beg)

I made them into mini muffins (4 dozen)... Baked for 25 minutes. 

Turned out yummy. :)

I didn't have sun-dried tomatoes, so I just quartered and sauteed them with the onions until all the juice was gone. I also subst. fresh basil from my garden & chopped that with the zucchini ...didn't bother to shred or drain that either. No hot sauce, so I subst. red pepper flakes. Subst. non-fat yogurt for the sour cream and olive oil for the butter. I did throw in a bit of parmesan, too. Inspite of all the substitutions, the muffins turned out moist & flavorful!

I did not have sun dried tomatoes or peppers. I did not shred the zucchini first because it was going into the food processor anyway and it worked great. My kids loved these. I made them as mini muffins so they could just pop them in their mouths. They were a little bland, but will definitely make them again.

Great recipe - used 1/2 cup nonfat yogurt instead of the butter and none of the oil. I also used whole wheat flour instead of all purpose and added 1 tbs. of flax seed to the mixture and it turned out just great. I got 20 muffins out of the recipe and calculated it at about 95 calories per muffin. I love it when I find a recipe that still tastes good using lower cal substitutions! I am sure that the original recipe tastes much better, tho!

this is a really good recipe. Muffins are tasty, moist and fragrant.
 I strictly followed the recipe except for the red peppers I can't eat; I substituted them with about 70 grams of minced speck, a typical italian smoked prosciutto.
as others suggested I mixed the parmigiano cheese into the batter.
I'll do these again!

Good muffin but a bit bland. The second time I made them (adjusted to a recipe for 11) I doubled the salt, mixed the parmesan in, and added 1/4 cup Kalamata olives. I also didn't pulse the zucchini. Still a bit dull and definitely not salty enough. Doubling the sundried tomatoes, olives, and hot sauce might help, and/or using a lot more or stronger cheese (feta?). I did use Greek yogurt in place of all the sour cream and two tbs of the butter and split the flour evenly between white and while wheat -- those changes worked well. As always since I live at 7000 ft. I had to make high altitude adjustments (the recipe adapted well to those adjustments). (Note that the first time I made them, I subbed sundried tomato pesto for the tomatoes -- not a good substitution at all, so I made sure I had the tomatoes on hand the second time.)

I didn't have sun dried tomatoes nor peppers but I improvised and added extra cheese, which I incorporated into the batter. I skipped the food processor part because I too like bits of veggies to be present so that step isn't crucial. One thing I would change next time-because there will be a next time , these are tasty!- I will also skip the sugar, not necessary and made them a tad too sweet for me. Great recipe that I will play with, for sure!

These muffins are wonderful - a bit time consuming but worth it. I cut the recipe in half (as there were only two of us eating) and got 9 muffins. Wish I would have made the whole batch because I bet they would freeze well. After cooking the onion and garlic, I threw the zucchini (and a little shredded carrot) into the pan for a couple of minutes to soften and then transferred to a strainer to cool. Did not pulse veggies in a food processor as the bits were already small. Mixed everything else as directed. I was tempted to add more moisture as the batter seemed a bit stiff but I didn't, and they turned out wonderful. These would be great with soup or chili. Will definitely make these again!
I like being able to see all the veggies so I skipped the food processor and subbed applesauce for butter

These are DELICIOUS! Was cooking for someone who's allergic to milk: substituted butter for olive oil, 1 cup Oatley Cuisine for the milk and sour cream and left out the parmesan cheese on the ones for our guest and it still turned out fabulous! This was a great way to get my kids enthusiastic about zucchini! Thank you so much!

**Update: Just made the recipe with all the dairy called for and it's fantastic this way as well! Couldn't even wait for it to cool down before eating one-- they smell AMAZING while they're baking!

8.7.20 ... https://www.allrecipes.com/recipe/204983/savory-zucchini-muffins/ ... What a production! 'Worth it! As DIZ said, it'll make your house smell like an Italian bistro! 'Only change was using oil from the sundried tomatoes instead of off-the-shelf oil. Light texture & subtle flavor. In twenty minutes, the twelve morethanfilled muffins were nicely rounded & ready. Thank you, ChristineM! Thank you, too, DIZ! ... Okay, Christine M. Okay, DIZ. My 23 had one; then, he had two more. He deemed them "Meat Muffins"! :D

These savory zucchini muffins are delicious! It’s hard to eat just one. My daughter brought me another zucchini from her garden & said more muffins please. The only I did differently was to use only all purpose flour, I didn’t have whole wheat. They have lots of flavor, especially if you follow the recipe!
I'd decrease the baking time by 5-10 minutes.

DELECTABLE! My house smelled heavenly while baking. Wouldn't change a thing; however, I did use roasted garlic because I had some in the fridge. Some of my ingredients were a smidgen over because after chopping and measuring, it just worked about that way. Was 1/4+ cup over with the zucchini and did not squeeze; never do--didn't seem to make any difference. Didn't have any whole wheat flour, used AP, but could see how it might add a little nuttiness. Stirred the Parmesan into the dry ingredients; and added the zucchini mix with the last half of the flour mix to minimize stirring. Mixed and chopped everything by hand. Filled the pan with 2 medium cookie scoops for each cup. They were golden and passed the toothpick test at 35 minutes. I adjusted the recipe for 9 servings because I only had the one 12-cup pan; sprayed with Pam, and everything easily fell out of the pan. Luckily for me I have more zucchini and will be making another batch real soon--like in a couple of days. Christine, I bet people love coming to your house for dinner. The flavors are amazing. Thank you for the wonderful recipe. These would be great as a mini-muffin appetizer for a party. Might try a little bacon next time?

I am making these for the second time today. I had brought them in for work and tomorrow we are having another celebration where I was forced to bring them again. No real force needed since they are indeed very good.
I used yoghurt instead of sour cream but otherwise just exactly the way it was described - and like others, took me longer to prepare. Perhaps with future use of recipe time will improve.

I replaced the zucchini with carrot pulp from my juicer (which worked well, as it was already dried out from the juicer). Not bad. Enjoy a glass of fresh carrot juice, then make some muffins. Delicious.
the prep listed is too convoluted - I streamlined the prep - great fragrance while baking and great taste when enjoying.

Made a few changes as suggested in other reviews such as 1/2 white and 1/2 whole wheat flour. Added 1/2 tbsp parmesan garlic dip seasoning from Epicure Selections and substituted 1/4 cup salsa for 1/4 of milk (so used 3/4 cup milk) Added in crushed chilies (about 1/2 tsp). So looking forward to having it with chili tonight.
